                                                           Dedication

                                                   O Worship the King

                                                   O worship the King, all-glorious above,
                                                   O gratefully sing His pow’r and His love;
                                                Our Shield and Defender, the Ancient of Days,
                                                Pavilioned in splendor, and girded with praise.

                                                    O tell of His might, O sing of His grace,
                                                 Whose robe is the light, whose canopy space;
                                              His chariots of wrath the deep thunderclouds form,
                                               And dark is His path on the wings of the storm.

                                                  The earth with its store of wonders untold,
                                                   Almighty, Thy power has founded of old;
                                                 Has 'stablished it fast by a changeless decree,
                                                 And round it hast cast, like a mantle, the sea.

                                                   Thy bountiful care, what tongue can recite?
                                                   It breathes in the air, it shines in the light;
                                               It streams from the hills, it descends to the plain,
                                                  And sweetly distills in the dew and the rain.

                                                   Frail children of dust, and feeble as frail,
                                                   In Thee do we trust, nor find Thee to fail;
                                                 Thy mercies how tender, how firm to the end,
                                                 Our Maker, Defender, Redeemer, and Friend!

                                                     O measureless Might! Ineffable Love!
                                                   While angels delight to hymn Thee above,
                                                 The humble creation, though feeble their lays,
                                                    With true adoration lisp to Thy praise.*

                                                                                                                             Robert Grant




* Underlining was added to indicate those attributes, characteristics, and descriptions of God that are also in this book.

There is something exceedingly improving to the mind in a contem-
plation of the Divinity. It is a subject so vast, that all our thoughts    According to the hymn Holy, Holy, Holy, God is "perfect in power,
are lost in its immensity; so deep, that our pride is drowned in its       in love, and purity." Indeed, the eternal God of the universe is in-
infinity . . . No subject of contemplation will tend more to humble        finite in Omnipotence, Lovingkindness, and Holiness.      Compiler
the mind, than thoughts of God…But while the subject humbles the
mind, it also expands it. He who often thinks of God, will have a          God's personality is so infinitely rich and manifold that it will take
larger mind than the man who simply plods around this narrow               1,000 years of close search and intimate communion to know even
globe . . . The most excellent study for expanding the soul, is the sci-   the outer edges of his glorious nature. 1                A. W. Tozer
ence of Christ, and Him crucified, and the knowledge of the God-
head in the glorious Trinity. Nothing will so enlarge the intellect,
nothing so magnify the whole soul of man, as a devout, earnest,
continued investigation of the great subject of the Deity…And, while
humbling and expanding, this subject is eminently consolatory. Oh,
there is, in contemplating Christ, a balm for every wound; in mus-
ing on the Father, there is a quietus for every grief; and in the influ-
ence of the Holy Ghost, there is a balsam for every sore…Would you
lose your sorrow? Would you drown your cares? Then go, plunge
yourself in the Godhead’s deepest sea; be lost in his immensity; and
you shall come forth as from a couch of rest, refreshed and invigor-
ated. I know nothing which can so comfort the soul; so calm the
swelling billows of sorrow and grief; so speak peace to the winds of
trial, as a devout musing upon the subject of the Godhead.
                                                   Charles H. Spurgeon

                        Bible Memorization and Prayer
The following illustration demonstrates how to prepare a complete Bible memory card including an example of a
prayer based on the living Word of God.

              FRONT  When I love and trust God fully,                                   Trust in the . . .
               SIDE    He directs my steps perfectly.

                         Proverbs 3:5-6

                         Pastor’s Sermon
                          God will not let us depart from
                          His will if we submit to Him.
                          Quote by Hudson Taylor
                          “God’s work done in God’s way will
                          not lack God’s supply.”                                        January, 2026



               BACK
               SIDE  Trust in the Lord with all thine heart;
                      and lean not unto thine own understanding.
                      In all thy ways acknowledge him,
                      and he shall direct thy paths.

                        Heavenly Father, I confess that I don’t always have the faith to trust You with all my
                         heart and that I even exalt human understanding over Yours. Holy Spirit, help me
                         to walk in the ways of the Lord and to fulfill all the purposes of God for my life to
                         the glory of God alone. I also ask that I will forever grow in my knowledge of You
                         and that I will love You and others more and more. In the Name of the Lord Jesus
                         Christ, I pray. Amen.



 Using a white 3X5-inch card, print neatly the Bible reference near the upper left-hand corner of the front side. A
    memory card is usually best prepared when the reference and the Scripture are on opposite sides and when there
    is only a single passage of no more than three or four verses. When reviewing or speaking Scripture, always repeat
    the reference along with its passage.
   Print a topical description or summary of the passage above the Bible reference.
   Print the introductory words or key phrases of the passage at the upper right-hand corner of the front side, if
    necessary to help with memorization.
   Print any pertinent comments and quotes below the Bible reference.
   Print the month and year at the lower right-hand corner of the front side when first memorized.
   Print the words of the passage by phrases on the back side of the card. (Just as song lyrics are best remembered by
    lines of words, so Scripture verses should be memorized by groups of words.) Review the card daily for one week
    and then once every month thereafter. Whenever any card from the monthly file is unsuccessfully reviewed, return
    it to the daily file for another seven days of repetition. Purpose also to review everyday by speaking or sharing
    memory verses in conversations, writings, and prayers. Let the Word of God be preeminent in everything you do
    and say.
   Print a personally relevant PRAYER below the passage.

           THY WORD HAVE I HID IN MINE HEART, THAT I MIGHT NOT SIN AGAINST THEE.                       Psalm 119:11
